# New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry

## SYNOPSIS

Builds one history value entry, for use with New-ZbxProxyData -History or Send-ZbxProxyData.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry [-ItemId] <ulong> [-Value] <string> [-Clock <DateTimeOffset>] [-Ns <int>] [-Id <long>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Writes a ZabbixProxyHistoryItem: sequence id, item id, clock, nanoseconds and value. It has no log-item fields (log timestamp, source, severity) and no not-supported flag; the server treats a value of exactly ZBX_NOTSUPPORTED as the item being not supported.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build one history value for an item

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value 42
```

One entry of a proxy's 'history data' array: the item's id, the value as text, and now as its clock (Unix seconds, with a stamped sub-second -Ns so two values in one second never collide). Id is a sequence number, auto-assigned.

### Example 2: Build a series with past timestamps

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
$start = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddMinutes(-5).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
0..4 | ForEach-Object { New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value (100 + $_) -Clock ($start + 60 * $_) } |
    Select-Object ItemId, Clock, Value
```

-Clock stamps each value (Unix seconds); -Ns and -Id may be given too when replaying stored data.

### Example 3: Take the item id from the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.status' | New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -Value 'degraded' |
    Select-Object ItemId, Value
```

-ItemId (and -Value, -Clock, -Ns, -Id) bind by property name, so an item from Get-ZbxItem supplies its own ItemId.

### Example 4: Put the entries into a proxy data request

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
$history = 1..3 | ForEach-Object { New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value $_ }
(New-ZbxProxyData -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Session ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N')) -History $history).History.Count
```

The entries are what Send-ZbxProxyData -History pushes, and what New-ZbxProxyData -History wraps for inspection.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixProxyHistoryItem`: One value as proxy data carries it: by item id, with its id — the store's sequence, which the server de-duplicates on — and its state.
